question: Should experimental grouped Claw updates be permitted to mutate package, config, and Gateway-owned resources before the project defines and proves an operator recovery flow and aggregate capability-escalation review?
rationale: The remaining question is not a narrow mechanical patch choice: it sets the acceptable safety contract for a multi-owner experimental lifecycle feature with external side effects.

options.title: Require recovery proof before merge
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed consent design, add an operator-facing recovery contract, and post redacted live evidence for package replacement, Gateway cron convergence, and retained-artifact recovery.

options.title: Accept a narrower experimental scope
options.body: Limit the initial update command to owners with proven reversible behavior and defer package or Gateway mutation until their recovery semantics are established.

options.title: Pause the apply stage
options.body: Keep the read-only planning work separate and defer mutation until RFC direction and lifecycle ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Require recovery proof before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed consent design, add an operator-facing recovery contract, and post redacted live evidence for package replacement, Gateway cron convergence, and retained-artifact recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identifies the unresolved operational contract and the evidence needed to accept it.
